thread:
alex: heads up — we saw a tiny but sharp spike of duplicate streaming sessions this morning, looks like reconnects are being interpreted as fresh sessions and the console is counting them twice. linking logs:```WARN sse: session resumed but new session_id created tenant=acme user=svc-123 route=eu-west-1```
sara: ugh. did that cause billing dupes or just console counts?
alex: console count doubled for ~3min for a subset of routes. billing pipeline seems ok (no double invoice), but the route-level traffic metrics showed two active sessions per connection for the same client id.
mike: repro steps? can we trigger locally with the proxy?
alex: yes — repro by forcing a midstream 204 from the edge, client reconnects right away, proxy sometimes hands off to a new route instance -> new session allocated. repro script:```curl -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' ... && kill -HUP proxy-pid```
jin: the core problem is the resume semantics + routing fallback. if route backend returns 204 midstream we create a new session token instead of reattaching to the existing lease. that behavior is working-as-coded but telemetry doesn't mark it as a resume vs fresh start. console just treats session_id presence as unique connection.
sara: so we need two changes: 1) mark events in telemetry as resume/fallback so console de-dupes; 2) consider changing routing to prefer resuming existing lease in same shard if possible.
mike: +1 on telemetry tags. we should add session_origin:resume|fresh and route_handshake:sticky|fallback fields so dashboards can filter.
jin: careful — adding too many tags will explode cardinality. propose a low-cardinality derived metric: resume_ratio per route and per tenant. tag allowed values: resume, fresh, unknown.
ops-bot: alert suppressed: streaming-duplicate-count spike resolved automatically at 2026-03-23T09:42:10Z
alex: for the console UX: can we show a small badge "resume vs new" in the connections table and a tooltip explaining why billing unaffected? product asked for that.
sara: yes, but need to be opinionated. simplest: compute dedup_key = tenant + client_id + short-window(10s). if two sessions with same dedup_key appear, mark as resumed in UI.
mike: that heuristic is ok for short bursts but will misclassify true parallel clients behind the same NAT. we should only apply deduping for streaming routes that support resume tokens. add feature flag to roll out.
jin: regarding rollout: feature flag + canary on 5% of tenants, monitor resume_ratio and false_positive_rate (measured by clients with distinct socket ip).
alex: for immediate triage can we patch telemetry to emit:```metrics.increment('sse.resume_event', tags={"tenant": tenant, "route": route, "outcome": "resume"})```
jin: implemented on branch sse/resume-tags — PR soon. but need console and alerting updates in parallel.
sara: i'll open a console PR to add the badge + filter; will include an opt-in toggle in settings.
mike: add runbook note: if resume_ratio spikes >10% post-rollout, rollback and investigate route affinity change.
alex: thanks. action items: alex: coordinate canary rollout plan + update alert thresholds; jin: finish PR for telemetry tags; sara: console badge + explainers; mike: add runbook and sampling checks.
jin: tagging @sre for visibility — we may want a retention tweak for resume logs (short term higher retention for 24h).
console-bot: ticket created: PLAT-8921 "sse resume telemetry + console badge" assigned to sara, jin, mike, alex
sara: pinging product for UX copy. @product could you review tooltip copy in PLAT-8921?
product: acked, will review by EOD
alex: ok let's aim for a canary tomorrow 09:00 UTC. I'll post status in #release-war-room when we start. :thumbsup:
